headline: LLM agents and structured models are assessed for biomedical reproducibility
label: Ai Agents For Biomedical Research
summary: Recent benchmarks show full-capability agents reproduce 60.6% of computational biomedical papers, prompting structured retrieval and process-level evaluation.
synthesis: The common thread is the evaluation of LLM agents and knowledge-structured or multimodal models on biomedical tasks, with emphasis on where they fail. ClaroAI-Bench reports that a full-capability agent reproduces 60.6% of computational papers in a 35-paper biomedical benchmark, while BiomniBench scores agent trajectories process-by-process on 100 data-analysis tasks against expert rubrics. A recurring design choice is added structure: scHilda integrates a knowledge graph into LLM reasoning for single-cell type annotation, S2F-Agent applies contract-based, human-in-the-loop orchestration to sequence-to-function workflows, and a cosine-similarity study argues typed-graph retrieval is needed because embeddings conflate EGFR L858R and T790M. Bio-BLIP and OmniGene-4 extend multimodal and mixture-of-experts designs to genomic variant interpretation and protein-homology tasks. What is new is the shift from outcome accuracy toward verifiable, process-level and interpretable evaluation.
